newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares recover from fall, but end lower.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares recover from fall, but end lower.

text.p: 1420 GMT - Firmer U.S. bonds helped Swiss shares recover from a fall in the early afternoon -- triggered by a slump in the dollar -- but they still ended below Tuesday's close.

Disappointment with the half-year figures of the three Swiss pharmaceuticals companies and Alusuisse had put shares under pressure from the start, but strong gains in Swiss Re had lent some support to the market.
* Swiss Market Index (SMI) index of leading shares fell 24.3 points, or 0.67 percent, to 3,697.7.
* All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) fell 12.40 points, or 0.52 percent, to 2,368.07.
Volumes in Roche, Ciba, Sandoz and Swiss Re were high. Market interest was slowly shifting from pharmaceuticals to insurers, a dealer said.

* Swiss Re was sought after the company announced on Tuesday the acquisition of Mercantile & General Re (M&G) from Prudential. Dealers said analysts may raise estimates for Swiss Re and further advances were likely. The rose 17 francs to 1,318.
* Ciba registered shares fell 27 francs to 1,538, Sandoz registereds were down 22 to 1,446. Dealers said half year figures released today were disappointing.

* Roche certificates lost 130 francs to 9,270 after Tuesday's half-year figures were at the lower end of expectations. A dealer added the downgrading by a U.S. broker also had a negative effect on Roche.
* The banks sector lost 0.7 percent on average.
* Alusuisse registereds down 20 at 943. Dealers said a first half profit rise of five precent was below expectations.
* Zurich followed in Swiss Re's footsteps, adding two francs to close at 334.
